name: The Christian walk
about: Separation, service, and walking with God.

teachings.title: Enoch walked with God
teachings.summary: Enoch, translated by faith and prophet of Christ's coming, is the example of walking separated and pleasing God, and the patriarchs picture the steps of coming to Christ.
teachings.text:
**And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.*

**Hebrews 11:5**
*By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.*

**Jude 1:14-15**
*And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.*

I've read that, when we look at these early patriarchs, we can see the pattern for salvation.

Adam knows God, his creator, and knows his sin. Abel brings the blood of atonement, given in faith for redemption. Seth and Enos, that with the mouth, confession is made, calling upon the name of the Lord. And with Enoch, we have the testimony that he walked with God, that he lived separated, pleasing God.

That each of us goes through these steps when we come to Christ and live for Him. An illustration given by God in His word, through the lives of these men.

But what of Enoch? The seventh from Adam (not to be confused with Cain's son, 3rd from Adam), Enoch was a prophet. A preacher, who gave witness in the Spirit to Christ's victory on the day of the Lord.

We know that by faith, he was transformed, translated that he should not see death.

But this is the promise to all saved by faith in Jesus.

**John 8:51**
 *Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.*

So what then? What does scripture mean by saying he was "translated?" That he was not found? Does it mean bodily ascension? Literally taken by God, not just his bodily death?

In **John 3**, Jesus says "*no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven,*" referring to Himself.

What then are we to take from this? Is there a hidden meaning to the story of Enoch? Can we dwell in ancient texts and Jewish fables searching for his fate? Certainly.

Lots of rabbi holes to go down with his story.

But what we can know from scripture is that Enoch walked with God, prophesying of Christ, and was pleasing to God. And draw inspiration to live in accordance to that ourselves, seeking to be similarly pleasing to God. In faith. In the Spirit. Not knowing death.

And that's really all that matters.

teachings.title: How to increase your faith
teachings.summary: Faith grows by hearing the word, doing it, praying for faith, and obeying God in things like church and tithing so that His kept promises teach us to trust Him more.
teachings.text:
How to increase your faith? The Bible tells us:

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

Read the word and listen to preaching from His word.

**James 1:22-24**
*But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.*

By living the word we begin to rely more of God and less on ourselves. The word becomes part of us, shoring up faith.

**Psalm 51:12-14**
*Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; And uphold me with thy free spirit. Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; And sinners shall be converted unto thee. Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: And my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.*

Pray for faith.

**Malachi 3:10**
*Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.*

God says to prove, or test Him. Obey His word (go to church, pay tithes in this example) and see how His blessings reward your faith in being a doer of the word. God keeping His promises is a huge way to learn to trust Him with more.

teachings.title: Beginning each day as the Lord's first fruits
teachings.summary: As the tabernacle was reared on the first day of the first month and the firstfruits belong to God, the believer gives himself to God daily, washed in Christ's blood and sanctified by the Spirit through his walk.
teachings.text:
**Exodus 12:1-2**
*And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying, This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.*

**Exodus 40:17**
*And it came to pass in the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was reared up.*

It has been a year for the children of Israel, a year since the passover and exodus from Egypt. A year in the wilderness, preparing all that God required; the covenant, the Tabernacle, the carnal ordinances and priestly vestments. The diverse washings and oils ready. The veil over the word of God, in the Ark at the heart of the Tabernacle.

And it is fitting on the first day of the first month that it is given to the Lord God as His. The first fruits are His. The first sons of Israel. The first of the flock. The first 10th of your earnings. All His. And as we begin each day as His, seeking first the kingdom of God.

**Luke 9:23**
*And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.*

**1 Corinthians 15:31**
*I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.*

We give to God ourselves daily. We put on the new man daily. We renew ourselves while we are yet in the flesh, beginning everything with God if we walk in the spirit.

And on that first day of the first month, Moses washed Aaron and his sons, anointing the vessels and sanctifying all, according to the word of God.

**Leviticus 20:7-8**
*Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy: for I am the Lord your God. And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am the Lord which sanctify you.*

**John 17:17**
*Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.*

**Hebrews 13:12**
*Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.*

**Romans 6:6**
*Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.*

We are washed in His blood, we are sanctified in the Spirit and we are made new daily, by our walk with Christ.

**Philippians 1:6**
*Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ*

teachings.title: Secret sin and the Father's rod
teachings.summary: God chastens His adopted children and brings secret sins to light, and the guilt of conscience should drive the believer to confess and forsake sin.
teachings.text:
Of course, David takes Bathsheba as his wife, one of many. He lives with his sin and the poor decisions he has made. But the Lord is displeased and David's actions won't remain hidden for long.

**Hebrews 12:6-7**
*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?*

**Hebrews 10:26-27**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

That fearful looking for judgment, the guilt we feel when we disobey God's word, the pangs of our conscience, is a powerful motivation to get right with the Lord. To call out to Christ our redeemer for forgiveness, to repent of our actions and seek to do the right thing. Especially knowing that, as adopted children, our Father will not spare the rod, and the sins we do in secret will be revealed in the light.

**Psalms 90:8**
*Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.*

**Proverbs 28:13**
*He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy*.

**Luke 8:17**
*For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.*

teachings.title: Seek ye first the kingdom of God
teachings.summary: Solomon building God's house before his own shows that those who seek God's kingdom first are blessed, not with a prosperity gospel but with fellowship and reward, as pillars in Christ's temple.
teachings.text:
Solomon built the House of God in 7 years, his own palace in 13. His zeal was towards the Lord.

**Matthew 6:33**
*But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.*

By seeking first the things of God, Solomon had the peace and blessings to them see to his own. The same promise to all believers, that in building up the temple of Christ, of which every believer is a pillar, we will be blessed in our lives.

**Mark 10:28-30**
*Then Peter began to say unto him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee. And Jesus answered and said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel's, But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.*

Not a "prosperity gospel," so much as a promise to be rewarded in our relationships with others, and the opening of their homes to those who do the work of the Lord. Fishers of men. Persecution and all, but we shall overcome.

**Revelation 3:12**
*Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name.*

The pillars Hiram made for the Temple, named *Jachin*—He will establish; and *Boaz*—in Him is strength, pictures of that Heavenly temple in which we are pillars of Christ's church.

teachings.title: Wisdom maketh his face to shine
teachings.summary: Walking with God and being anointed by the Spirit changes a believer's countenance and gives boldness to preach the truth, so that others see they have been with Jesus.
teachings.text:
The Preacher continues his sermon. Having said he has searched for wisdom by observation of all things under the Sun, and having found all have sinned and fallen short. That the wise and the fool, the rich and the poor, all are appointed to die, and after this, judged and found wanting, that then the only way is God's. That fear of Him and seeking His favor is the only alternative to the vanity and vexation of spirit that man travails in.

Solomon begins **Ecclesiastes 8** praising the effect that seeking God's wisdom has on us. That it makes the face to shine, and to speak boldly His truth. That it changes the countenance of a person to walk with God.

**Exodus 34:29-30**
*And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses' hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him. And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.*

Moses had to cover his face from the people, it disturbed them so much to see the radiance coming from his time with God.

**Psalm 104:15**
*And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man's heart*.

The Spirit is described as oil, which anoints us as we walk in Him. The bread, His word. Our heart, merry from the juice of the vine, which is Christ. He does make our faces shine. His light magnified through us, that men see us and know, we have been with Jesus. And the boldness of our wisdom comes from the confidence we have in Him and His word.

The Spirit filled the disciples of Christ, gathered in the upper room on Pentecost, and having His anointing, they went out among the multitudes gathered for the feast in Jerusalem, and preached with boldness.

Acts 2:1-4
*And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance*.

The men, hearing the miracle of preaching Christ from scripture, in their own tongues, languages from around the known world, they wondered; *Behold, are not all these which speak Galilaeans?* But the disciples had been changed by their time with God. The boldness to preach Christ from scripture, and 3,000 souls came to repentance.

Just as when Peter and John were brought before the religious leaders of the Jews for preaching Christ, these lowly fishermen gave witness that they had been with Christ by their boldness.

**Acts 4:13**
*Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.*

Their light so shined, that others saw and praised God. The anointing of the Spirit, the truth of God's word, the wisdom they trusted, gave them boldness to preach the truth. They were changed.

The understanding that man's countenance gives away their time with God to others, has a counterpoint in scripture. That the reprobate, those that hold the truth in unrighteousness, have a similar change;

**Isaiah 3:9**
*The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.*

We should seek to walk with God, to be anointed with the Spirit, that men look upon us and take note that we have been with Jesus. To speak boldly the wisdom of the gospel. To make known the truth of His way.

teachings.title: The bride who would not open
teachings.summary: The bride who delayed to open to her beloved pictures saved believers who grow complacent and make excuses when God calls them to His work, and so lose His fellowship and suffer His chastening.
teachings.text:
Chapter 5 opens with the aftermath of the close of the previous chapter, which ended with the woman calling upon her bridegroom, her lord.

The spiritual moment of acceptance and humility, asking Him for salvation. Opening yourself to be intimately known of God.

Verse 1 gives the bridegroom's POV. Having entered the garden, come unto his dearest sister, his spouse, gathered the spices and ointments of myrrh, eaten the sweet of the honeycomb, drunk the wine and milk, and calling those at the wedding feast, and his bride, to eat and drink, abundantly.

**Revelation 22:17**
*And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.*

This picture of salvation, the immediate joy and celebration, the call to get your fill of an abundance of the sweet and precious food and anointing oils, wine and milk, to drink abundantly, is God's call to us to now walk in His Spirit. To take full advantage of the relationship His children have with the Father in Christ, the true King. The Shepherd. The Bridegroom. Not a thief, but our Savior.

**John 10:10**
*The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.*

We are called to walk in the Spirit and receive the fruit thereof;

**Galatians 5:22–25**
*But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law. And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.*

This initial feeling of having come to a feast and being overwhelmed with the love of God towards us, His blessings and rest, is marvelous. But we may tire and sleep in that contentment.

The bride sleeps, but her heart wakes. She hears a knock. A voice. It is her beloved, calling to her to let him in. He asks her to open to him, *my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled*. He has come, his hair wet with the dew of the night to see her.

He is Christ come to give His bride a blessing, but she doesn't leap to open the door.

She makes excuses; *I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?* Rather than hear His voice and do His will, that we may be blessed, a believer may see their contentment and undefiled spirit as a bed to rest upon. When God asks so little of us whom He has saved, to open when He knocks, will we respond?

**Revelation 3:20**
*Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.*

In the Christian life, God gives us works to do. Poor to be fed. A gospel to be preached. Divine appointments to be kept. His burden is light. He wants so little from us, yet in our own selfish interests, we make excuses. Taking for granted all He has given us.

And, even as the beloved reaches his hand in through the door, making that extra effort to stir his bride, God will try and overcome our hesitation, moving in our lives.

His effort stirs her. She rises but too late. She feels the sweet smelling myrrh, the holiness of Christ, upon the lock. But, He has withdrawn.

When we don't respond to God's callings, and hesitate to do His will, He will give us a taste of life without Him. He will lift His hedge of protection. He will let us suffer consequences He has spared us from. He will chasten every son.

The bride's soul fails, knowing she did wrong and desperately she seeks her beloved, in the very manner she once sought him. Wandering in the dark streets, calling for him. Trying to find her own way.

This time, the watchmen find her and persecute her. The smote her and wound her and remove her veil of purity. She suffers for her love's sake.

The watchmen who could not tell her the way to her love in chapter 3, now treat her wickedly.

teachings.title: I am my beloved's
teachings.summary: The bride's choice to rise early and go forth with her beloved pictures the mature believer deliberately making Christ the centre of each day and working with Him to bear fruit in new believers.
teachings.text:
Song of Solomon 7 opens with the King, having called his beloved Shulamite woman to return to him that he may look upon her at the end of chapter 6, now detailing what he sees of his beloved. He describes her beauty and the perfect symmetry of her body.

*How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!*

Everything he sees of her is good. Just as we are seen as perfect and without spot when God looks upon us, clothed in the righteousness of Christ.

**2 Corinthians 11:2**
*For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.*

**Colossians 1:22**
*In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

**Jude 1:24–25**
*Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.*

The woman responds to her husband, her brother, her spouse with unwavering confidence;

*I am my beloved’s, and his desire is toward me.*

We are Christ's, and His desire is for us.

Beginning there in verse 10, she responds to her beloved, knowing she is his, and inviting him to go forth with her, to live with her. To get up early to the vineyards, to see the vine flourish and come to fruition, where she will give him her love.

The spiritual application here; She has gone from her initial humble acceptance of his love, to the joy of the wedding feast, to her period of complacency, persecution, profession of faith and renewal, to now making the decision to plan her day and life around him, is a beautiful picture of the Christian life.

A believer makes the conscious decision to make Jesus their companion. To go forth with Him and to reside with Him. To wake early in the morning, starting the day with Christ, and His word. In prayer.

This intentionality is contrasted with the bride laying in bed, hesitant to wake, making excuses to avoid letting in her beloved. As mature Christians, in it for the long haul, we seek Him first.

We work with Him to tend the vine, which is His church, bringing forth fruit which are new believers. Planting the seed of His word. Watering and nurturing. Tending to them, the babes in Christ, and helping them grow to maturity. Through it all, giving Him all our love.

We lay up our fruit, those people we have given the gospel to, the needy to whom we give comfort. The broken hearted we have consoled. This treasure we have laid up for Heaven, but to Him is the increase. We give Him our all because He is our beloved.

teachings.title: No want to them that fear Him
teachings.summary: God provides for those who fear Him and live righteously, chastens those who do not, and expects believers to love the brethren by not forsaking the assembling of the local church.
teachings.text:
*O fear the LORD, ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.*

Believers, sanctified in the Spirit by faith in the risen Christ, are given the promise that the Lord will redeem us, His servants.

But His provision for us extends beyond the fact of eternal salvation, and gives us hope and comfort here, in this life. Our daily bread, shelter, clothing, we shall not want for any good thing.

But more, He's given us His word, and His standards for separation that we may fear the Lord and be blessed by having a longer life and see good within the years we are allotted.

His burden is light. Don't speak evil of others, don't lie. Don't seek to harm others, but do good and seek peace.

**Romans 12:18**
*If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.*

Vengeance is Mine, sayeth the Lord. He will repay. We not only believe He is, and a rewarder of those that diligently seek Him, but that He is our shield and strength against our enemies. We do not need to fight a battle, but trust in Him to fight for us. We simply need to walk in the Spirit, love our enemies, hate His, and seek others' profit. Doing good.

If we want our Father's blessing, live righteously. He hears the righteous and answers their cry.

We are known by our love for the brethren. By our edifying one another.

**Hebrews 10:22–25**
*Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

You don't want the face of God against you in your time of need.

**Hebrews 10:26–29**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries. He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?*

God will chasten His children. He will shorten your life and withhold blessings, and even bring you home for not doing His work at His pleasure.

**Hebrews 10:31**
*It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.*

Note that we are expected to love and care for our fellow saints. And where do we do this? On the called out assembly of believers. Our local church. Forsaking this opportunity is spiteful to the Spirit of grace which has bought you. Go to church!

teachings.title: He that is chief, as he that doth serve
teachings.summary: Like David's mighty men and the disciples striving for position, believers may strive to do great things for the Lord, but first must seek to serve, counting the cost of suffering while pressing toward the prize.
teachings.text:
This chapter reminds me of the Apostles, constantly competing for position and favor and honor in the Kingdom of Heaven.

**Luke 9:46-48**
*Then there arose a reasoning among them, which of them should be greatest. And Jesus, perceiving the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by him, And said unto them, Whosoever shall receive this child in my name receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same shall be great.*

**Luke 22:24-30**
*And there was also a strife among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest. And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors. But ye shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve. For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am among you as he that serveth. Ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations. And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.*

**Mark 10:35-45**
*And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come unto him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall desire. And he said unto them, What would ye that I should do for you? They said unto him, Grant unto us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glory. But Jesus said unto them, Ye know not what ye ask: can ye drink of the cup that I drink of? and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? And they said unto him, We can. And Jesus said unto them, Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of; and with the baptism that I am baptized withal shall ye be baptized: but to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give; but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared. And when the ten heard it, they began to be much displeased with James and John. But Jesus called them to him, and saith unto them, Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them. But so shall it not be among you: but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: and whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all. For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.*

The Apostles and chief disciples of Jesus were as the mighty men of David. And we are called honor as well. We can do great things for the Lord, even strive with one another to out do each other. We can run the gauntlet of Philistines to bring water for our Lord, but first we should seek to serve. First we should seek to be a good judge for the children, the fatherless, the widows. A servant to our brethren.

And we should be cautious in what we strive for, as the sons of Thunder, James and John sought. The baptism of pain and persecution may be the price for glory. The cup of tribulation and suffering for His name. But even so, we should reach for the prize set before us;

**1 Corinthians 9:24-27**
*Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain. And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible. I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air: but I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.*

**Philippians 3:13-14**
*Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.*

teachings.title: Heap coals of fire on his head
teachings.summary: Unlike Jonah, believers must show mercy to enemies, including giving them the bread of life and water of the gospel, remembering the mercy God showed them.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 5:44-45**
*But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.*

**Romans 9:15-16**
*For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.*

**Proverbs 25:21-23**
*If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee. The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.*

Perhaps the hardest thing in the Christian life, showing mercy to those who hate us and whom we hate. But if God chooses us to be a blessing to another, it isn't on us to question why. We shouldn't be as Jonah.

And if they are hardened against us, that's on them. Our mercy will be as hot coals upon their head.

**Romans 12:20**
*Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.*

Note the spiritual application of this. Your enemy hungers and thirsts. For what? Food and water? Or truth and the repentance unto faith in Christ?

Will the coals of fire make them angrier and dug in against you? Or remind them of the Hell that awaits them?

Will you withhold that bread that came down from Heaven? The waters of life that you've drank?

Are there many who don't know their right hand from left?

Only God knows.

Remember the mercy God showed you, and let that be what guides your spirit. Don't be as Jonah, and let your anger consume you.

teachings.title: Usury and forgiving our debtors
teachings.summary: God's people should not take usury or unjust gain from the poor but give cheerfully and forgive debts, as God has forgiven us.
teachings.text:
This even extended to making a profit on food sold to the poor;

**Leviticus 25:35-37**
*And if thy brother be waxen poor, and fallen in decay with thee; then thou shalt relieve him: yea, though he be a stranger, or a sojourner; that he may live with thee. Take thou no usury of him, or increase: but fear thy God; that thy brother may live with thee. Thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor lend him thy victuals for increase.*

Land owners were expected to allow gleaning of their fields, that after a harvest, the poor should go through the fields and bring in anything left behind by the laborers.

Alms and feasts of charity are expected of the Lord's people. Forgiveness of debts. A cheerful giver, providing for those in need is praised.

**Proverbs 11:25-27**
*The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself. He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.*

As **Proverbs 28:8** promises;

*He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor*.

The gain you may make is temporary. The Lord will make certain your wealth is distributed to the righteous, in the end.

Because God is so just to forgive us, we should love one another enough to be like Him.

**Luke 7:41-42**
*There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty. And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?*

So, we should not seek unjust gain, and further, we should relieve those in our debt, as God has forgiven us.

**Matthew 6:9-13**
*After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.*

teachings.title: Defend the widow and the fatherless
teachings.summary: God's call to defend and provide for the widow, the fatherless and the needy is the outward practice He expects of believers, and He desires this mercy rather than the vain rituals and sacrifices of works-based religion.
teachings.text:
The reoccurring theme of the Lord defending the widow, the fatherless and the poor, and our role in carrying out righteous judgment for them, is probably the most talked about doctrine outside of Who God is, and the doctrines of salvation in Christ.

More than anything else, we are to clothe and feed the truly needy, to make sure people don't take advantage of those who have no one to defend them. No husband, no father. To do unto the least of these, and in doing so, doing it for Jesus.

**James 1:27**
*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

This is the ultimate expression of our faith. The outward practice God expects. Self-sacrifice for others, not the selfish sacrifice of the works-based religions of the world.

**Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings*

All the penance and "Eucharist" sacrifices, and all the other rites and rituals men do to get the Lord to be pleased with them are vain. God wants us to exercise mercy and judgment.

**Proverbs 21:3**
*To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.*

Jesus, reading Isaiah, gives us the mission statement for Christians;

Luke 4:18–19
*The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.*

Amen

teachings.title: Delight in the saints, not Lordship salvation
teachings.summary: Calling Jesus Lord is a saved believer's statement of fact, not the false gospel of Lordship salvation; our good works add nothing to God but are poured out in love and service to the saints.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 16** presents another sacred hymn celebrating the Lord's salvation, the eternal security of the believer, and the promise of the risen Christ.

The preservation of the saints is the hope of all who place their trust in God. Our very being cries out to Him for salvation, recognizing He is Lord.

Note here that this isn't "Lordship salvation," a false gospel that says you must "make Jesus the Lord of your life" to be saved. It is saved believers, already trusting Him to save us, recognizing that He IS the Lord, as a statement of fact.

David writes, *Thou art my Lord: my goodness extendeth not to thee; But to the saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent, in whom is all my delight.* The good that we do isn't for Him, it adds nothing to the holy and perfect God.

The idea that Jesus needs us to make Him Lord, that by our "turning from sin," we justify ourselves before God, is hubris. It's a false gospel.

The good we do comes from Him, and is poured out to the brothers and sisters, the saints. We benefit others, and they glorify God. We obey His judgements, to one another's profit.

**Matthew 5:16**
*Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.*

We submit ourselves to the righteousness of God. We do not seek to establish our own righteousness, but to magnify His.

**Romans 10:3–4**
*For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

David's burden is for the saints in the earth, his delight is to the excellent of God. Just as we are commanded to.

**John 13:34–35**
*A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.*

While we should seek to live peaceably with all men, we should especially look with love upon our fellow believers.

**Galatians 6:9–10**
*And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.*

This is the message that we have heard from the beginning. It is our job as Christians. It is how we are to know one another. Not keeping to ourselves or seeking out own profit. Certainly not by hating our brothers.

1 John 3:10–11
*In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.*

This is the mind of Christ, to be servants, one to another. To delight in others.

The ultimate expression of humility isn't thinking less of yourself, but not thinking of yourself at all. And the humbleness of submission to God's righteousness should naturally turn to our service for others. Not to add to God's goodness our filthy rags, but to glorify His goodness in us.

teachings.title: The desires of thine heart
teachings.summary: When we trust the Lord and do good, our heart's desires become His, turning from our own lusts to pure religion and good works done for others so they glorify God.
teachings.text:
God promises those that trust in Him and do good will be given the desires of our hearts.

**Jeremiah 17:9–10**
*The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it? I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.*

When we are right with God, and do according to His ways, our heart's desires are His. They are upright and good, because our will becomes His when in all our ways we acknowledge Him, and allow the Lord to direct our paths.

He tries the reins, and sees our good works and rewards us openly. We consider the poor and broken-hearted. We take up the cause of the fatherless and widows. We spread the good news of eternal life in Christ Jesus. We live lives separated unto the gospel, and consider the profit of others above our own. Our desires become for the good of others.

*Lord help me to live from day to day*
*In such a self-forgetful way,*
*That even when I kneel to pray*
*My prayer shall be for others*.

This hymn encapsulates the concept.

**James 1:27**
*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

When we consider others, when we love our neighbors and even our enemies, when we practice pure religion, the outward works of our faith, it should be for others.

And our keeping ourselves from the filth of the world is part of that, that God will see our good works, and give us our desires, and make all things come to pass.

*He shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday.*

We are the light of the world. Our purpose is to magnify the light within us that others, yes others, see it and glorify God.

**Matthew 5:16**
*Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.*

By trusting the Lord and doing good, we preserve our nation, we get to dwell in the land, we are fed, and we see our hearts turn from desiring our own wicked lusts, to seeking good for others.

teachings.title: Blessed is he that considereth the poor
teachings.summary: God blesses those who help the poor out of unfeigned charity rather than to be seen, because the heart behind the giving is what He rewards.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 41** is brief and to the point. David opens with the doctrine of the Lord's promise to preserve and give long life on the earth to those of His people who consider the poor. Who show mercy to the widows and take up the cause of the fatherless.

Just as the commandment to honor your parents comes with a promise, that it be well with you and lengthen your days, this practice of pure religion, to consider the poor, comes with a similar blessing.

Basic stuff, which we are told over and over again in scripture, because it often is the hardest thing for man to do; love the unlovable the way God loves us.

**Luke 14:13–14**
*But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just*.

The act of giving alms or feeding the poor is not itself what gives us blessings. Many may be generous in their actions, to be seen of men or to make themselves self-righteous.

Helping people who cannot help you back out of love, is love unfeigned. It is the charity Paul calls us to. The selfless, sacrificial love for God and others, in your heart. More so than the actual alms or donation of goods. The spirit behind it is everything.

**1 Corinthians 13:3**
*And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.*

So we see that the love behind the care given to the poor, is rewarded with strengthening us in our sickness, delivering us from our enemies, God showing to us the mercy we showed those who could never repay us for the kindness.

Those that do it for their own reasons, have their reward. But the heart behind it is what God wants from us.

**Matthew 25:40**
*And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me*.

**Proverbs 19:17**
*He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.*

God loves a cheerful giver, one who isn't seeking anything for himself.

**Proverbs 22:9**
*He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.*

But those that oppress the poor, God hates.

**Proverbs 14:31**
*He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the needy*

teachings.title: Bloom where the Lord has planted you
teachings.summary: Like Jeremiah, who longed to flee to the wilderness but was sent to preach at the temple gates, Christians are not to retreat to compounds but to be a light where people are, enduring tribulation with hope because Christ has overcome the world.
teachings.text:
*Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.*

**Jeremiah 9** continues his prophesying, the hard preaching of the words of God against the children of Israel that remain in Judea.

And in it, the lamentation to seek to flee from Jerusalem and the wickedness of this generation, and go to the wilderness, to live off grid, and be away from the evil people, uncircumcised in the heart.

But God calls upon Jeremiah to preach in the city, by the gates of the Temple. To tell them of the pending destruction their forsaking Him has brought up on them.

This same impulse is given to Christians today. To flee the world, to get to a redoubt in the wilderness. To be far from the fallen society that, like just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.

But, like the prophets, and like Christ Himself, we go to Jerusalem. We are called to go to the population centers and preach the acceptable year of the Lord. To seek that which is lost. To be a light in that darkness.

We can't be a light to others if we are hidden in the woods.

And so we are in the world, not of it.

Rather than coveting a RETVRN to a past we never knew, or a rustic compound in the hills, we are supposed to bloom where the good Lord has planted us. To be a blessing to those around us. To *be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ*.

Not to flee persecution, and the tribulations that come to every believer, living for the Lord. To *glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.*

**James 1:12**
*Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.*

**Romans 8:18**
*For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.*

**James 1:2-4**
*My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.*

We who believe on Christ have already overcome this fallen world. Because He has overcome death and Hell for us. We shouldn't be black pilled. We may wail with lamentations for our people to repent, but standfast in the faith that has saved us.

**John 16:33**
*These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.*

teachings.title: God is a God of separation
teachings.summary: From creation onward God separates and divides to make a holy people, separating believing Israel after the Spirit from unbelieving Israel after the flesh, wheat from chaff, until the harvest is complete.
teachings.text:
Here we go.

God is a God of separation. The Bible has example after example of division, separating one thing from another. Day from night. The creatures after their own kind. Woman from man. Man from the Garden. Cain and Abel. The descendents of Seth, the sons of God that called upon the name of the Lord and the children of men who did not. Noah and his perfect generations from fallen man. The animals of the ark. The nations of Noah's sons. The people of Babel and their languages. The habitations of the nations. Abraham out of Ur. Ishmael and Isaac. Jacob and Esau. Joseph and his brothers. Hebrews out of their land and into Egypt. Out of Egypt and back in the land. The covenant with Moses that they would be a holy people. Separated from other nations.

Even here, in Numbers, each tribe separated and counted. And the Levites separated even further.

**Luke 12:51**
*Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:*

The division. The separation. Making holy a people of God. Separating Israel from Judah. And Jesus from the root of Jesse. Believing Israel from the non-believing Jews. The tares from the wheat. Sheep from goats. Israel after the flesh and Israel after the Spirit. Unfruitful branches cut off and cast into the fire. The election in Christ chosen to be graft in.

**Deuteronomy 7:6**
*For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God: the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.*

**Isaiah 62:12**
*And they shall call them, The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken.*

**1 Peter 2:9**
*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light;*

Winnowing the chaff from the wheat. The earth is His threshing floor. The harvest is ongoing. We are in the last days, and have been since the first fruit of Christ, and the harvest of 5,000 made by the disciples on Pentecost. We shall bring in the sheaves for the Lord. To Him the increase. Until the fullness of the harvest comes in.

Amen

teachings.title: When family despises your walk with Christ
teachings.summary: As Michal despised David's worship, worldly loved ones may resent a believer's walk with Christ, and Jesus warns that family and the cares of this world must not come before discipleship.
teachings.text:
**Numbers 4:15**
*And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the vessels of the sanctuary, as the camp is to set forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. These things are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation.*

Poor Uzzah. If only he had been a Levite of the line Kohath.

David builds the tabernacle in his city, and his houses and settles the ark of the Lord in Jerusalem. Leading the congregation with music and singing. Glad to be going to the house of the Lord.

But Saul's daughter, Michal, David's first wife, looks upon him and despises him.

The hatred of Michal towards David is personal, obviously their turbulent history and his taking her father's place act as kindling for it. But the spark seems to be seeing David gladly worshipping the Lord. Joining in the assembly. Getting right and doing things for God.

In a like manner, we may often experience this reaction as saved believers, where a family member or someone close to us resents our relationship with Jesus and our going to church, reading the Bible, cleaning up our life.

Bringing the word of God, the holy Spirit, the love of Christ, into our lives can make worldly people despise us.

Jesus came to bring division.

**Luke 14:26-27**
*If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.*

A man may come to Jesus, and despise not his wife or family, and so, not be a disciple. A believer can be saved and yet be caught up in the cares of this world, being influenced by others who pull him away from living for Christ.

**Matthew 13:22**
*He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.*

If you seek to be more than just be saved, a good husband and father, wife and mother, but instead wish to do great things for the Lord, don't neglect Jesus' warning.

And as Paul wrote, in his opinion; **1 Corinthians 7**:

*It is good for a man not to touch a woman. Nevertheless, to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband. Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.*

*But I speak this by permission, and not of commandment. For I would that all men were even as I myself. But every man hath his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that.I say therefore to the unmarried and widows, it is good for them if they abide even as I.*

Marriage is honorable. Family is a blessing. But be aware that your commitment to Christ can put you at emenity with your loved ones. Division; **Luke 12:53:**

*The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.*

teachings.title: Building the wall while the mockers scoff
teachings.summary: Like Nehemiah's builders, believers growing in sanctification will be mocked even by family, and must keep building, put on the whole armour of God, and pray for one another.
teachings.text:
And so as the construction continued, and the mockers increased their scorn and ridicule, it became apparent to the scorners, like Sanballat, a governor in Samaria, Tobiah the Ammonite, that the Jews were serious in the endeavor.

The wall wasn't finished but it was getting there.

In our Christian life, we may experience initial scoffing by our friends, family and neighbors. People who doubt our conversion because they know us. The old man. And those things they say may throw us off our course. Make us doubt ourselves.

When Tobiah says a fox could topple their wall, it's like when a brother or parent scoffs at our faith and our attempts to get right. But we see from Nehemiah how to handle this. To turn their reproach upon their own head. To trust in the Lord.

Their mocking comes not only at our expense, but it reveals in themselves to their own sin and iniquity.

**Proverbs 29:27**
*An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.*

Jesus says He came into this world to divide it. Even family.

**John 3:19-21**
*And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.*

So the scoffers in Nehemiah's day set their minds to violence in an effort to stop the construction. This also can be how some people will react to your sanctification, as you build upon the foundation Christ has laid in your heart. So we must stand watch, and continue building. We put on the whole armor of God.

**Ephesians 6:10-18**
*Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand. Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace; Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints*

The prayers of the saints are our spears, always at the ready. Pray for one another to stand strong to the mocking. Our brothers and sisters in Christ. Knowing we have each other's back, as the people of Jerusalem did against the mockers.

teachings.title: Be not envious against evil men
teachings.summary: Solomon's later proverbs read like Paul's epistles in teaching believers not to envy or keep company with evil men nor partake of their sins, showing the single unified wisdom of God throughout the Bible.
teachings.text:
Deep in the meat of the word, the heart of these sayings, we really can capture the themes that have been being hammered, again and again, and see the Gospel of hope that is in Proverbs.

To me, these later sections seem almost to be a New Testament epistle, and much of it would fit there.

The Epistles of Paul highlight the implications of salvation on the Christian life. Solomon's wisdom does much the same thing.

**2 Corinthians 6:14**
*Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?*

Be not envious of evil men, or desire to be with them. Don't take part in another man's sin.

**1 Timothy 5:22**
*Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure.*

**1 Corinthians 5:11**
*But now I have written unto you not to keep company, if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.*

**Ephesians 5** is full of such wisdom;

*Let no man deceive you with vain words: for because of these things cometh the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience.Be not ye therefore partakers with them*...

*And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them.*..

*See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord is. And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit*...

*Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.*

The wisdom of God is clear and consistent throughout the Bible. We are given parable, story, sayings that all convey a single, unified message. The way of God. His ways are not our ways, yet we may know Him, because He has shown us in His word. What a blessing.

teachings.title: Should New Testament Christians take vows
teachings.summary: Christ and James command not to swear, so believers should live consecrated lives daily without vows, keeping an honest testimony as a witness for the gospel.
teachings.text:
But should we as New Testament Christians take vows?

**Matthew 5:33-37**
*Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.*

**James 5:12**
*But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.*

We are already called to live consecrated lives in service of the Lord. Separated unto the Gospel. And as such, are supposed to be dedicated to the purposes of God without vow, but as His.

And in doing so, we see that the more important thing is that our testimony be without question or ill repute. Blameless. Honest in our dealings that when we say to someone the reason for our hope, we are a good witness for the Gospel that they might be saved.

And while times of fasting or dedication to a specific task for God may be something we do for specific favor, or time offered in service for thanksgiving, we should live separated lives daily, with joy and thanksgiving.

**Psalms 61:8**
*So will I sing praise unto thy name for ever, that I may daily perform my vows.*

teachings.title: Don't make a vow you cannot keep
teachings.summary: God will exact the price of any vow made in His name, so it is no sin to refuse to vow, and plain honesty with yea and nay is the better way.
teachings.text:
*When thou shalt vow a vow unto the Lord thy God, thou shalt not slack to pay it: for the Lord thy God will surely require it of thee; and it would be sin in thee. But if thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee.*

**Matthew 5:34-37**
*but I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil*

**James 5:12**
*But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation*.

**Ecclesiastes 5:4-6**
*When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay. Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?*

**Exodus 20:7**
*Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.*

People who "swear to God," who make promises to God they cannot keep, who make promises to others based on the righteousness of Christ, swearing on a Bible, and all other manner of ways to vow a vow, need to be careful. God is very clear that He will exact the price for your vow. So don't make one you cannot keep.

There is no sin in refusing to vow in His name. And as Christ tells us, being honest in all your dealings is a much better policy. Let your yea be yea and your no, no.

teachings.title: Words are the window to the heart
teachings.summary: The righteous are vexed by the wicked words of the world, and as Jesus taught, what comes out of the mouth reveals and defiles the heart, so believers must watch what they say.
teachings.text:
David's plea for help, like many of the Psalms, comes from the vexation of spirit in dealing with the wicked of this world. That in a world where believers, Christians, are called to be separated and holy as He is holy, the fallen world full of the iniquity of man troubles us. It is the lot, no pun intended, of the believer.

**2 Peter 2:6–9**
*And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;) The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished*

This is a feeling we can all relate to, if you walk in the Spirit.

The vexation is not just bearing witness to the unlawful deeds of the wicked, but in *hearing* them as well.

David says they speak vanity to each other, and flatter, and with a double-heart, speak lies. They pridefully boast. It is the wickedness of words that sees David cry out.

**Matthew 12:34–37**
*O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things. But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.*

Jesus shows us that words are the window to the heart of a man. An evil heart brings forth evil words, and it is those words that condemn them.

**Matthew 15:10–11**
*And he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.*

This understanding, that it wasn't the ritual washings and dietary laws, cleaning the outside of the cup -but the heart, and what proceeds out from it though the mouth, that makes a man unclean, is often neglected by Christians, today. But one of the most repeated commands in scripture is to watch what you say.

Proverbs is full of advice to remain silent, to not speak like the fool or the froward. To speak truth in all things. To refrain from vain, useless speech.

But the wicked refuse to hear God's word and follow His way. Men *Who have said, With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own: who is lord over us?*

Of course, by admitting they have power over their own tongue, they condemn themselves.

teachings.title: Playing church versus mercy
teachings.summary: God is not pleased with outward acts of religion, ritual and showy worship but with a humble heart and mercy to the lost, the poor and the widow.
teachings.text:
Today, many Christians worry more about the outward acts of religion over the spiritual things of God. They play church, and make a long pretense of prayer, and get into "worship services," getting ecstatic over worldly sounding music, or engaging in fasts and other rituals, that satisfy their needs and excite the flesh, but do nothing for honoring God or doing what He has commanded us.

Dead works and vain traditions, but no mercy or judgment for the lost, the poor, the widow, the fatherless.

**Luke 18:12-14**
*I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess. And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.*

**Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

**Matthew 12:7**
*But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.*

God doesn't care about where you sit in church, sitting in the chief seats, or your religious acts that show everyone else how holy you claim to be. But He cares about what's in your heart and how you treat others.

You can be the most separated person in the pews, but if you look down on others, and hold yourself as better than, you're separated unto yourself. Not the gospel of God. Like these men who inquired of the Lord.

teachings.title: The charge of formalism
teachings.summary: As God indicted Israel for keeping outward forms while failing to declare His law and show mercy, Christians covered by Christ's once-for-all sacrifice must not be hypocrites but do the good works they were saved for.
teachings.text:
Now, having been summoned to His judgment, and having stipulated His position, God begins the indictment against His people, giving the matters of His suit, which He Himself will judge.

God, in showing that He has no need for the blood of bulls and goats, fowls or anything else, begins by laying the charge of formalism against His covenant people.

The religious practices are being maintained, the bare minimum of service to keep the covenant. The Lord isn't accusing them of failing this aspect, but in the weighter matters, as Jesus accused the Pharisees.

God established promises and practices to maintain them as His people, but they are failing to declare His statutes, or to proclaim His law.

The entire point of Israel was to be a light to all men. Not to selfishly reap the benefits while doing nothing to teach all nations as an example.

**Deuteronomy 4:5–6**
*Behold, I have taught you statutes and judgments, even as the LORD my God commanded me, that ye should do so in the land whither ye go to possess it. Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.*

They had squandered their blessings by not fulfilling this role.

**Matthew 15:8**
*This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.*

God is directly accusing the wicked among His people of missing the entire point, a charge Jesus will use to indict the religious leaders of the Jews.

**Matthew 23:27–28**
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness. Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.*

As an application for Christians today, the indictment is the same leaven of the Pharisees; hypocrisy.

**Hebrews 10:8**
*Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law*.

Just as the Pharisees had the OT sacrifices, we have the once and for all sacrifice of Christ, and total remission of sins.

**Hebrews 10:17–18**
*And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more. Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.*

Just as He says to His people That he isn't seeking to add more sacrifice to those that they are already, God isn't asking us for additional acts of atonement. He remembers our sins no more. There is no more sacrifice to be had.

**Hebrews 10:26–27**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

Just like Israel in **Psalm 50**, we are covered by the blood. We are his people. But are we bound by the formalism and outward appearance of being clean, while failing to maintain the good work that God has saved us for? That gives Him glory?

Or are we looking over our shoulder, expecting a similar charge to be made by God against us as He is making here?

If we're not declaring his righteousness and glory in Thanksgiving, and showing mercy and judgment to others, loving our neighbor, how are we taking his covenant in our mouths? How are we telling the world that we are Christians when we aren't acting like it? Who does it benefit?

**James 2:14–17**
*What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him? If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.*

teachings.title: Pay thy vows and plead His promises
teachings.summary: God holds us to the vows we make in His name, yet He delights when we remind Him of His promises in prayer, and in Christ we have boldness and access to ask of the Father.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 28**
*And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the Lord be my God:*
*And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.*

The moment of truth. Will God deliver or will Jacob be killed? And if he puts his full trust in God, recognizing His power, having faith he will be delivered safely to his father's house in peace, he will have to honor his vows.

Sometimes we as Christians, especially when we haven't been walking with Christ, maybe backslidden or just stubbornly trying to fix and control things in our lives, we will make vows to God if He would provide. God holds us to the vows we make in His name.

**Numbers 30:2**
*If a man vow a vow unto the LORD, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word, he shall do according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth*

**Ecclesiastes 5:4**
*When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed*.

**Psalms 76:11**
*Vow, and pay unto the LORD your God: let all that be round about him bring presents unto him that ought to be feared.*

At the same time, God delights in our reminding Him of His promises, in prayer and supplication. Because God is not slack concerning His promises. He keeps His side of every covenant. And our acknowledging of this and trusting Him to do so brings Him joy and glory. It is not tempting God to remind Him, by our recognition, realizing all He does is in grace and mercy to us, as sinners, that He is true to His word and won't let us down.

And in Christ we have the authority to boldly go before the Father, and all we ask shall be delivered.

**Ephesians 3**

*8 Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ;*

*9 And to make all men see what is the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ:*

*10 To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God,*

*11 According to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord:*

*12 In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.*

*13 Wherefore I desire that ye faint not at my tribulations for you, which is your glory.*

*14 For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,*

*15 Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named,*

*16 That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;*

*17 That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love,*

*18 May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height;*

*19 And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.*

*20 Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,*

*21 Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.*

teachings.title: Our bad report and hardened hearts
teachings.summary: Hebrews warns that saved believers who fall back into dead works can give the lost cause to harden their hearts until it is too late, so Christians bear a grave responsibility to walk righteously so that any rejection is the unbeliever's own fault.
teachings.text:
One of the key points throughout the book of Hebrews is that if we who are saved fall back again to the old ways, to the sin offerings and dead works, to bitterness at reproach, to neglecting our Christian walk, we bring others down with us, who have not received salvation. Who haven't yet come to the saving faith. Who may be pricked by the Spirit and hear the power of God's Word, and so taste of the heavenly calling and fall short by our example. And *thereby many be defiled.*

Especially knowing that there comes a point where their rejection of the truth and refusal to find faith in the hope we have can leave them reprobate. Either in death, or by being turned over to a reprobate mind by God. We give them cause to harden their hearts. To be dull of hearing. To not believe our report.

Our faith alone cannot bring another to the knowledge of the truth. But our lack of faith can lead the lame to stumble, as we bring them to uneven paths, leaning on our own understanding.

Many of us harp on the Reprobate Doctrine because it is an extremely important Biblical truth that far too many are ignorant of, or reject to lean on their own understanding or follow the wisdom of men. There is a point where it is too late for some. And once they are given up and given over, they are twice-dead. Children of Hell, fit for burning.

But this isn't simply for the cursing of those who have been rejected by way of their hardened heart, but a grave warning to those of us who have been blessed by the faith in God's promise and redeemed in the blood of Christ.

Faith comes by hearing the word of God.

So does reprobation. The Bible says they have the knowledge of the truth but don't wish to retain God in their knowledge. That they turn the truth of God into a lie.

If they will harden their hearts and turn away from the truth, don't let it be that we, like David, *despised the commandment of the LORD,* and give *great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme.*

Don't let it be by our bad report.

Rather, if they reject the truth of God and His offer of grace and mercy, let it be because by our righteous conversation. Our behavior. That they see our faith and that we walk the straight paths, and if it offends them so be it. If our separation from the things of this world and the peace we have because of the blessed hope we've attained offends them, then it's their own dull hearing and seared conscience to blame.

This is a great responsibility.

teachings.title: Millstone warning to reprobate pedophiles
teachings.summary: From Luke 17 he teaches that reprobate sodomites recruit by offending children and that Jesus tells them they would be better drowned, then applies the warning against offending others to believers too.
teachings.text:
Luke 17 continues the portion of the Gospel where Jesus preaches and teaches, making His way to Jerusalem. Here, again addressing His disciples Jesus says "*It is impossible but that offenses will come."*
